text:
Season 1 Overview (Story Setup)
The story unfolds over several months in a world where seasons last for years. In the Seven Kingdoms of Westeros, the long summer is ending and winter approaches. Lord Eddard “Ned” Stark of Winterfell is summoned by his old friend King Robert Baratheon to become the new Hand of the King after the sudden death of the previous Hand, Jon Arryn (Ned’s mentor and father-figure). Ned is reluctant but accepts after learning Arryn may have been murdered; he plans to investigate using his new authority.

Across the Narrow Sea in Essos, the exiled Targaryen siblings Viserys and Daenerys (children of the Mad King Aerys II, overthrown by Robert) plot their return. Viserys arranges for Daenerys to marry Khal Drogo, leader of a massive Dothraki horse-lord army of tens of thousands, in exchange for warriors to invade Westeros and reclaim the Iron Throne. Daenerys seeks safety more than power.

At the northern edge of the realm, the Night’s Watch guards the massive ice Wall against wildlings and darker threats from the lands of always-winter. Rumors of ancient evils stir. The season follows these three main threads—the political intrigue and family conflicts in Westeros, the Dothraki journey and rising power of Daenerys, and the Watch’s grim duties—as they intertwine toward war, betrayal, and change.
1

Season 1 Episode 1: Winter Is Coming
Beyond the Wall, three Night’s Watch rangers—Ser Waymar Royce, Will, and Gared—ride into the Haunted Forest to check reports of wildlings. Will, the best scout, finds a group of wildling corpses arranged in a strange pattern and a dead girl pinned to a tree. He reports back. Gared urges caution and a return to Castle Black, but young Ser Waymar insists on seeing the bodies. When they arrive the corpses have vanished. A tall figure with ice-blue eyes—a White Walker—appears and easily kills Waymar. Gared tries to flee and is beheaded. Will watches in horror as the dead wildling girl rises as a wight with glowing blue eyes. He flees south in terror.

In Pentos, Viserys Targaryen prepares his younger sister Daenerys for marriage to Khal Drogo. He is harsh and controlling, inspecting her body and insisting she must please the Khal so he can gain an army. Daenerys bathes in scalding water without flinching. Drogo arrives, looks her over briefly from horseback, and rides off; Illyrio Mopatis reassures Viserys this means approval. Daenerys does not want the marriage, but Viserys threatens her and says he would give her to the entire khalasar if it meant reclaiming the throne. At the wedding celebration there are deaths in fights (normal for Dothraki). Gifts include books from the exile knight Ser Jorah Mormont (who swears to Viserys), three ancient petrified dragon eggs from Illyrio, and a white mare from Drogo. That night on the beach Drogo consummates the marriage roughly; Daenerys is frightened and in pain.

In King’s Landing the bells toll for Jon Arryn’s death. Queen Cersei Lannister worries that Arryn discovered something dangerous and may have told someone. She confides in her twin brother Jaime of the Kingsguard. He tells her not to worry—if the King knew their secret they would already be dead. Cersei wants Jaime as the new Hand; he has no interest in the work.

In the North at Winterfell, Ned Stark watches his young son Bran practice archery with help from older brothers Robb and the bastard Jon Snow. Little sister Arya shows better aim. News arrives of a Night’s Watch deserter. Ned takes Robb, Jon, Bran, ward Theon Greyjoy, and guards to carry out the sentence himself with the great Valyrian steel sword Ice, teaching Bran that the man who passes the sentence must swing the sword. The deserter Will begs them to warn of White Walkers before dying. Ned dismisses it as madness—the Walkers have been gone for thousands of years.

On the ride home they find a dead stag and a dead mother direwolf killed by an antler. Five pups survive. Jon argues it is an omen—the direwolf is the Stark sigil and Ned has five trueborn children—so the pups are taken home. Jon finds a sixth albino runt and keeps it. Later a raven brings word of Jon Arryn’s death and that King Robert’s court is riding north. Ned realizes Robert will ask him to be Hand. He does not want to leave Winterfell.

The Stark children name and bond with their growing direwolves: Grey Wind (Robb), Lady (Sansa), Nymeria (Arya), Summer (Bran), Shaggydog (Rickon), and Ghost (Jon). Bran is caught climbing again as the royal party approaches. The courtyard fills for the arrival. King Robert greets Ned warmly and immediately demands to visit the crypts to pay respects at Lyanna Stark’s tomb (Ned’s sister, once betrothed to Robert). Cersei is impatient. Jaime finds their younger brother Tyrion (a dwarf) in a brothel with the prostitute Ros and hauls him to the feast. In the crypts Robert still rages about Rhaegar Targaryen “kidnapping” Lyanna and says not all Targaryens are dead. The episode ends with the threads of family duty, hidden secrets, ancient threats, and forced alliances all set in motion.
2

Season 1 Episode 2: The Kingsroad
The Dothraki khalasar leaves Pentos and rides into the vast grassy Dothraki Sea. Viserys stays with them, impatient for his army. Jorah explains he is an exile because he sold poachers into slavery and fled Ned Stark’s justice. Daenerys struggles with her new life and Drogo’s rough nightly visits; she finds some comfort looking at her dragon eggs. Her handmaiden Doreah teaches her how to take control in bed and gain her husband’s respect rather than submit like a slave. Daenerys begins speaking Dothraki and using her body differently; Drogo responds more gently.

At Winterfell Bran lies unconscious after his fall. Tyrion forces a reluctant Joffrey to pay respects to the Starks. Tyrion tells his family he will ride north to see the Wall before returning south and notes Cersei and Jaime’s guarded reactions when he says Bran will live. Cersei visits Catelyn at Bran’s bedside and shares the story of her own first son (a black-haired boy) who died of fever, offering to pray for Bran.

Jon has a light sword forged for Arya; she names it Needle. He tells her “stick them with the pointy end” and says goodbye. He kisses the comatose Bran farewell. Ned says goodbye to Jon, promising to tell him about his mother next time they meet and affirming he is a Stark by blood even without the name. The parties split: Ned, Arya, Sansa and the royals south on the Kingsroad; Jon, Tyrion and Benjen Stark north to the Wall.

On the road Robert tells Ned that spies report Daenerys has married Drogo and the khalasar is huge. He fears another war. Ned points out the Dothraki have no ships. Robert presses Ned about Jon’s mother; Ned stays silent.

Back at Winterfell Catelyn refuses to leave Bran’s side. A fire is set as a distraction; an assassin tries to kill the boy with a Valyrian steel dagger. Catelyn fights him off until Summer the direwolf kills the man. Later Catelyn finds a long blonde hair in the tower where Bran fell. She gathers Robb, Theon, Maester Luwin and Ser Rodrik and concludes the Lannisters tried to silence Bran because he saw something. She decides to ride south secretly to warn Ned, leaving Robb in charge with Rodrik as escort.

On the northern road Jon and Tyrion talk. Tyrion says books are his weapons. New recruits (criminals who chose the Wall over mutilation) join them. Tyrion warns Jon the Night’s Watch is full of broken men, not heroes. They reach the Wall; its sheer size impresses even Tyrion.

At the Inn at the Crossroads the royal party stops. Joffrey takes Sansa walking by the river. They find Arya practicing swordplay with the butcher’s boy Mycah. Joffrey torments the boy with his sword Lion’s Tooth. Arya hits him with a stick; Nymeria bites Joffrey’s arm. Arya throws the sword in the river and runs. Sansa is torn. Later before the King, Joffrey lies about the fight. Sansa, pressured, will not contradict him. Cersei demands a direwolf’s death. Nymeria has fled (Arya drove her off with a rock), so Lady is killed instead on Robert’s reluctant order. Ned does the deed himself. The Hound returns with Mycah’s corpse, saying the boy ran but not fast enough. Far away in Winterfell, Bran finally wakes.
3

Season 1 Episode 3: Lord Snow
The royal party reaches King’s Landing. Ned is immediately called to a Small Council meeting. He meets Jaime in the throne room; old bitterness over Jaime killing the Mad King (who murdered Ned’s father and brother) surfaces. The council members are: Petyr “Littlefinger” Baelish (Master of Coin, who knew Catelyn as a girl), Grand Maester Pycelle, Renly Baratheon (Robert’s younger brother, Master of Laws), and the eunuch Varys (Master of Whisperers). Ned learns the crown is six million gold dragons in debt—half to Tywin Lannister—and Robert has ordered an expensive tournament to celebrate Ned’s appointment. Ned wants to cancel it; the others doubt the King will listen.

Cersei coaches Joffrey: when he is king the truth will be whatever he says. She warns him the North cannot be easily conquered and that anyone who is not a Lannister is an enemy. She tells him to be kind to Sansa for now.

Arya and Sansa are still angry over the river incident. Ned explains Sansa was trapped and gives Arya permission to keep practicing with Needle. He hires the Braavosi water dancer Syrio Forel (former First Sword of Braavos) to train her. Watching them, Ned realizes his daughter may be preparing for real conflict.

Catelyn and Rodrik arrive secretly but are spotted by Littlefinger’s men and taken to one of his brothels, where Varys also waits. Littlefinger reveals the assassin’s ornate dagger once belonged to him—he lost it betting against Tyrion Lannister. He fetches Ned; after a tense moment Ned is reunited with his wife. He vows to expose the Lannisters. Littlefinger offers help for old affection toward Catelyn.

News of Bran’s recovery reaches the city. Cersei fears exposure; Jaime comforts her. Robert trades war stories with Barristan Selmy and jokes with Jaime about the Mad King’s last words (“Burn them all”).

At Winterfell Bran is awake but paralyzed and remembers nothing of the fall. Old Nan tells him dark tales of the Long Night and White Walkers instead of heroic stories. Robb confirms he will never walk again; Bran says he would rather be dead.

At Castle Black Jon dominates the training yard against the other ragged recruits. Ser Alliser Thorne mocks him as “Lord Snow.” Tyrion watches with Lord Commander Jeor Mormont. Later the other boys jump Jon; Tyrion stops it and tells Jon he is alienating them by being better trained and standoffish. Benjen refuses to take Jon ranging yet—rank means nothing here; everything must be earned. Benjen leaves on a ranging. Tyrion talks with Mormont and the ancient blind Maester Aemon; they beg him to ask the court for more men. Aemon warns winter is coming harder than anyone remembers and darker things than wildlings may come with it. Tyrion climbs the Wall, urinates off the edge (an old ambition), shares a moment with Jon, and departs south with recruiter Yoren.

In the Dothraki Sea Daenerys boldly orders the khalasar to halt. Viserys is furious and threatens her; a bloodrider whips him and forces him to walk in shame. Irri tells Daenerys she is pregnant. She shares the news with Drogo; they hope for a boy. Jorah and Rakharo discuss fighting styles. Jorah leaves briefly for Qohor on business but will rejoin before Vaes Dothrak.
4

Season 1 Episode 4: Cripples, Bastards, and Broken Things
At Winterfell Bran dreams of a three-eyed raven. Tyrion (passing through with Yoren) gives Bran designs for a special saddle that will let him ride by voice and reins alone, saying he has a soft spot for “cripples, bastards and broken things.” He does it partly to repay Jon’s earlier friendliness. Robb allows him to stay but Tyrion prefers the town brothel. Theon is rude; Tyrion needles him about being a glorified hostage.

At Castle Black soft, fat, fearful Samwell Tarly arrives. Thorne and the others mock him mercilessly as “Ser Piggy.” Jon protects him, fighting multiple boys at once. Sam explains his father Lord Randyll Tarly gave him a choice on his eighteenth nameday: take the black or suffer a convenient “hunting accident.” Jon is shocked a trueborn son could be treated worse than a bastard. That night Jon uses Ghost to intimidate the bully Rast into going easy. Next day no one will fight Sam hard. Thorne is furious and later describes a blizzard beyond the Wall that forced cannibalism. Jon and Sam clean together and admit neither has been with a woman; Jon does not want to risk fathering another bastard.

In Vaes Dothrak the khalasar arrives at the sacred city (no walls, only a horse-statue gate). Viserys is angry they are going the “wrong” way. He bathes with Doreah and rants about dragons and destiny. Later he storms into Daenerys’s tent when she invites him to dinner (he sees it as being commanded). He insults her Dothraki clothes and gifts. She fights back for the first time, hitting him with a belt and warning that if he ever strikes her again he will lose the hand. She tells Jorah she now sees Viserys will never be a real king.

In King’s Landing Sansa visits the Iron Throne room with Septa Mordane and frets about producing heirs and Joffrey’s lingering anger. At the Small Council Ned hears of rising crime from the coming tournament crowds and lends men to the City Watch. He questions Pycelle about Jon Arryn’s final days. Pycelle says Arryn borrowed a thick book of noble lineages and his last words were “the seed is strong.” Ned takes the book. He finds Arya practicing balance and tells her Bran can still have a full life as a lord or counselor even if he cannot be a knight; when she asks if she can do those things he says she will marry a lord and have sons. She replies that is not her.

Littlefinger advises Ned to keep the investigation quiet and points him toward Jon Arryn’s former squire (now a knight fighting in the tourney) and an armorer. Ned’s man Jory is rebuffed by the arrogant new knight Ser Hugh. At the smithy Tobho Mott, Ned meets the apprentice Gendry, who made a fine bull’s-head helm. Jon Arryn had visited and asked about Gendry’s mother. Looking at the boy’s face Ned realizes Gendry is one of Robert’s bastards. He does not yet understand why Arryn cared. Later Jory tries to deliver a message to Robert and finds Jaime on guard outside while the King beds other women; Jaime is bitter and reminisces with Jory about the Greyjoy Rebellion.
5

Season 1 Episode 5: The Wolf and the Lion
Catelyn’s party (with Tyrion as prisoner, plus sellsword Bronn and others) rides through the Vale. She has been loudly claiming they are going to Winterfell as misdirection. Hill tribes attack; Tyrion fights and kills a man, saving Catelyn’s life. They reach the Eyrie. Lysa Arryn (Catelyn’s sister) is unstable and furious that Tyrion has been brought there. She sends him to a sky cell—a three-sided room open to a sheer drop. Tyrion must sleep carefully or roll to his death.

At Winterfell Bran is frustrated by his mother’s absence and his paralysis. Maester Luwin suggests he learn a short bow for mounted shooting. Theon is with Ros and bristles when she compares him unfavorably to Tyrion.

In King’s Landing Ned questions Barristan Selmy about Ser Hugh’s sudden death in the lists (Hugh had expensive new armor right after being knighted). Robert wants to joust himself; Ned points out he is too fat for his armor and the knights would let him win. The tourney begins. Ser Gregor “the Mountain” Clegane faces Ser Loras Tyrell (the Knight of Flowers). Loras rides a mare in heat that distracts Gregor’s stallion; Gregor is thrown, beheads his own horse in rage, and attacks Loras. Sandor Clegane (the Hound, Gregor’s brother) intervenes. Robert stops the fight. Loras names the Hound the victor.

Varys privately tells Ned that Robert will soon be dead unless Ned saves him, that Jon Arryn was poisoned with the Tears of Lys for asking questions, and that Ned is one of the few honorable men left. Arya chases cats into the dungeons and overhears Varys meeting with Illyrio Mopatis. They discuss how the lion and wolf will soon be at war (as planned), but it has come too soon—Drogo will not invade until his son is born. Illyrio suggests killing Ned; Varys refuses. Later Varys and Littlefinger trade veiled threats about each other’s schemes.

Yoren arrives with urgent news of Catelyn’s arrest of Tyrion. At a Small Council meeting Robert learns Daenerys is pregnant and orders her, the child, and Viserys assassinated. Ned refuses on principle and resigns as Hand. Robert is furious. Renly and Loras (lovers) discuss Renly claiming the throne himself with Tyrell support; Renly is fourth in line and hesitant. Cersei and Robert share a rare drink and talk about the Targaryen threat and Lyanna; their marriage was doomed from the start.

Littlefinger takes Ned to a brothel to show him another of Robert’s bastards—a baby girl with black hair. Leaving, Ned and his men are ambushed by Jaime and Lannister guards. Jaime demands answers about Tyrion. Fighting breaks out. A Lannister guardsman stabs Ned through the leg; Jory is killed. Jaime leaves Ned wounded in the street.
6

Season 1 Episode 6: A Golden Crown
Ned wakes from his injuries. Robert restores him as Hand and orders him to make peace with the Lannisters before leaving on a hunt. Cersei is furious; Robert strikes her when she insults him. Arya trains with Syrio even while grieving Jory; Syrio teaches that one must be ready to fight especially in dark times.

On the hunt Robert drinks heavily (kept supplied by Lancel Lannister) and waxes nostalgic; Renly storms off. Back in the city refugees report a huge knight (the Mountain) burning Riverlands villages—Lannister retaliation for Tyrion’s capture. Ned strips Gregor of titles and lands and sends Lord Beric Dondarrion with men to bring him to justice. He summons Tywin Lannister to court or be named traitor. Littlefinger and Pycelle are alarmed at the escalation.

Joffrey apologizes to Sansa (on Cersei’s earlier orders) and gives her a necklace; she forgives him. Ned decides to send the girls home. Sansa protests she will marry Joffrey and have golden-haired babies. That phrase sends Ned back to the lineage book. Every Baratheon-Lannister match produced black-haired children—except Cersei’s three blond ones. He realizes the truth.

At Winterfell Bran rides with his new saddle. Robb and Theon discuss war rumors. Bran wanders off and is attacked by wildlings. Robb kills two; Theon shoots the third who holds a knife to Bran. The survivor Osha yields and is taken prisoner. Ros leaves for King’s Landing, correctly sensing war will empty Winterfell of customers.

At the Eyrie Tyrion nearly rolls out of his sky cell. He bribes the jailer Mord to take a message. Lysa brings him to court expecting a broken confession. Instead Tyrion demands a trial. Since Lysa’s son Robin is a child, Tyrion claims trial by combat. He first names Jaime (absent), then accepts any champion present. Bronn volunteers. In the fight Bronn uses speed and terrain against the heavily armored Ser Vardis Egen, kills him, and kicks the body out the Moon Door. Tyrion is free. He and Bronn leave.

In Vaes Dothrak Daenerys tests a dragon egg in fire; she is unburned while Irri is scalded. She eats a raw stallion heart before the dosh khaleen. The crones prophesy her son will be the Stallion Who Mounts the World. She names him Rhaego after her dead brother. Viserys is jealous. He later tries to steal the dragon eggs; Jorah stops him. Drunk and furious at a feast, Viserys draws a sword in the sacred city (a capital offense) and demands his crown. Drogo “crowns” him by pouring molten gold over his head. Viserys dies screaming. Daenerys watches coldly and says he was no dragon.
7

Season 1 Episode 7: You Win or You Die
On the Riverlands border Tywin Lannister has raised 60,000 men. He tells Jaime this war will make or break their house for a thousand years. He orders Jaime to take half the army and besiege Riverrun. Even the “least” Lannister (Tyrion) must be avenged or the family looks weak.

At Winterfell Theon tries to bully Osha; she is unimpressed. She tells Maester Luwin the wildlings fled south because the White Walkers have returned. Luwin is skeptical.

At the Wall Benjen’s horse returns without him. Jon and the other recruits take their vows. Jon is assigned as Lord Commander Mormont’s personal steward (not a ranger); Sam becomes Maester Aemon’s steward. Sam suggests it may be so Mormont can groom Jon for command. Jon (who keeps the old gods) and Sam swear before a heart tree beyond the Wall. Ghost finds a severed hand in the woods.

In Vaes Dothrak Daenerys tries to persuade Drogo to invade Westeros for their son’s future throne. Drogo is uninterested in an “iron chair.” In the market a wineseller offers her poisoned Arbor gold (an assassination ordered by Robert). Jorah, who has just received a royal pardon via one of Varys’s little birds (realizing he is no longer needed as a spy), stops her from drinking. The seller is captured. Enraged, Drogo vows to cross the “poison water,” take the Iron Throne for his son, and kill the usurper’s men. The khalasar leaves the next day, dragging the wineseller to death.

In King’s Landing Ned confronts Cersei with the truth: her children are Jaime’s, not Robert’s. She does not deny it and is proud, comparing it to old Targaryen custom. She has hated Robert since their wedding night when he called her “Lyanna.” Ned tells her to flee with the children before Robert returns. She warns him: “When you play the game of thrones, you win or you die. There is no middle ground.”

Littlefinger coaches new prostitutes (including Ros) and recounts his past duel for Catelyn and his realization that he must win by cunning, not honor. He wants “everything.”

Renly finds Ned: Robert has been mortally wounded by a boar on the hunt. Ned goes to the dying king. Robert names Ned Protector of the Realm until Joffrey comes of age and asks him to stop the hit on Daenerys. Ned writes “the rightful heir” instead of Joffrey’s name. He does not tell Robert the truth about the children, sparing him. Varys hints that Lancel kept Robert drunk. Renly offers Ned swords to seize Joffrey now; Ned refuses to shed blood while Robert still lives and insists Stannis is the true heir. He writes to Stannis. Littlefinger urges a quieter path—control Joffrey as a puppet or switch to Renly later—but Ned calls it treason. Littlefinger agrees to “help” secure the City Watch.

Robert dies. Ned is summoned to the throne room. Joffrey sits the Iron Throne and demands fealty. Ned presents Robert’s decree. Cersei tears it up and offers Ned a chance to bend the knee and go home. He refuses and orders the City Watch to seize the queen and her children. Instead the gold cloaks turn on Ned’s men. Littlefinger holds a knife to Ned’s throat: “I did warn you not to trust me.”
8

Season 1 Episode 8: The Pointy End
At the Wall Jon and Sam bring back two corpses from Benjen’s party (Jafer and Othor). The bodies do not smell of rot. Mormont wants Maester Aemon to examine them first. News arrives that Ned has been arrested for treason. Jon is devastated; Mormont reminds him of his oath. Alliser Thorne taunts him; Jon attacks and is confined. That night Ghost alerts him. A wight (the reanimated Othor) attacks Mormont’s chambers. Jon’s sword does nothing; he finally destroys it with fire from a lamp. The bodies are burned. Sam has read that only fire kills wights raised by White Walkers.

In the Vale Catelyn is furious that Lysa did not warn her of Ned’s arrest and will not send the knights of the Vale to war. Lysa cares only for her son’s safety. Tyrion and Bronn, free, are captured by hill tribes led by Shagga. Tyrion talks fast, promising them gold, weapons, and vengeance against the Arryns if they help him reach his father. They agree and escort him west.

In the North Robb receives a letter (dictated by Cersei via Sansa) demanding he bend the knee. He refuses and summons the northern banners. At a feast Greatjon Umber challenges Robb’s authority; Grey Wind bites off two of his fingers. Robb turns the moment into dark humor and wins the Greatjon’s fierce loyalty. Robb says goodbye to Bran and Rickon. Osha tells Bran the Old Gods are real and the real war is in the north against what is coming, not the south. Catelyn and Rodrik intercept Robb’s host. She tells him he must win for the family’s sake. They debate strategy: Tywin’s army or Jaime’s at Riverrun. To reach Jaime they need the crossing at the Twins (held by Walder Frey). A Lannister scout is captured and sent back with a message that 20,000 northerners are coming.

Tyrion arrives at Tywin’s camp with the hill tribes. Tywin shows little warmth but accepts the fighters—on condition Tyrion leads them from the front.

Tyrion arrives at Tywin’s camp with the hill tribes. Tywin shows little warmth but accepts the fighters—on condition Tyrion leads them from the front.

In Lhazar the Dothraki raid a peaceful village for slaves and loot to fund ships. Daenerys is horrified by the rapes and killings and claims the remaining women as her own to protect them. An angry warrior named Mago challenges Drogo; Drogo kills him but takes a deep chest wound. Daenerys insists the Lhazareen healer Mirri Maz Duur treat it despite the bloodriders calling her a maegi (witch).

In King’s Landing Lannister men slaughter the Stark household. Septa Mordane tells Sansa to run; the Hound takes Sansa. Ser Meryn Trant and men interrupt Arya’s lesson. Syrio sees they are not Ned’s men. He holds them off with a wooden sword, telling Arya to run: “The First Sword of Braavos does not run.” Arya flees to the stables, finds Needle, and accidentally kills a stableboy who tries to stop her. She escapes via the tunnels. Varys visits Ned in the black cells. He is shocked Ned warned Cersei. Ned’s mercy, Varys says, got Robert killed. Catelyn no longer holds Tyrion, so there is no hostage to trade. Varys serves “the realm.” Cersei’s council forces Sansa to write a letter begging Robb to bend the knee, implying Ned’s life depends on it.
9

Season 1 Episode 9: Baelor
Robb’s army reaches the Twins. Catelyn negotiates with the elderly, lecherous Lord Walder Frey. In exchange for crossing, troops, and support, Robb must marry a Frey daughter and Arya must marry a Frey son; Robb also takes a Frey squire. He agrees.

Tywin plans to use the hill tribes as expendable vanguard and puts Tyrion in front. Tyrion is given the whore Shae by Bronn. The night before battle they play a drinking game. Tyrion tells the story of his secret youthful marriage to Tysha (a common girl Jaime had set up as a kindness). Tywin had the marriage annulled, revealed she was a prostitute, and forced Tyrion to watch as his guards raped her for silver. The memory still wounds him.

Next morning the Starks have stolen a march. Tyrion’s speech to the tribes is cut short when he is knocked unconscious. He wakes to learn the Lannisters “won” a diversionary fight, but Robb’s main force smashed Jaime’s army at the Whispering Wood, lifted the siege of Riverrun, and captured Jaime himself. Robb refuses Jaime’s offer of single combat and has him chained. Two thousand of Robb’s men died in the feint; he tells the army the war is far from over.

At Castle Black Mormont gives Jon the Valyrian steel bastard sword Longclaw (once meant for his own exiled son Jorah) in thanks for saving his life. He is sending Alliser Thorne south with a wight hand as proof. Sam tells Jon that Robb is marching to war. Jon wants to go. Blind Maester Aemon reveals he is Aemon Targaryen—he had to stand by while his family was slaughtered in Robert’s Rebellion. Duty is hard; Jon must choose and live with it.

In the Dothraki Sea Drogo’s wound festers. He falls from his horse—a terrible sign. Daenerys stops the khalasar and has Mirri Maz Duur treat him. The bloodriders are furious. Jorah arms himself and warns Daenerys that when Drogo dies his rivals will kill her and the baby. She refuses to leave. Mirri begins a blood magic ritual, sacrificing Drogo’s prized stallion. As supernatural noises rise from the tent, Qotho attacks Daenerys; Jorah kills him. Daenerys goes into labor. No Dothraki midwife will help the “cursed” woman, so Jorah carries her into the tent.

In King’s Landing Varys urges Ned to confess treason so he can take the black and save Sansa’s life. Ned is torn. Arya lives rough on the streets, catching pigeons. She hears the Hand is being taken to the Great Sept of Baelor and climbs a statue of King Baelor for a view. Ned sees her and mouths “Baelor” to Yoren, who understands and moves to grab her. On the steps Ned looks at both daughters and chooses to save them. He falsely confesses that he betrayed Robert and that Joffrey is the true king. Joffrey pretends he will be merciful and send Ned to the Wall (as Cersei and Sansa begged), then suddenly orders his head instead. The crowd riots. Yoren pulls Arya away and shields her eyes. Sansa screams and faints. Cersei and Varys try to stop it too late. Ser Ilyn Payne uses Ice to behead Ned Stark. Pigeons fly up; Arya knows.
10

Season 1 Episode 10: Fire and Blood
In King’s Landing Ned’s head is mounted on a spike. Yoren cuts Arya’s hair, calls her “boy,” and takes her into a group of Night’s Watch recruits (including Hot Pie, Lommy, and Gendry—Robert’s bastard, now cast out). He warns her half the recruits would sell her to Cersei. They leave the city heading north through war zones. Joffrey has a singer’s tongue cut out for an offensive song, then forces Sansa to look at her father’s head and promises her Robb’s next. She quietly says maybe Robb will give her Joffrey’s. He has Meryn Trant beat her. The Hound quietly wipes her blood and advises her to give the king what he wants. Cersei takes Lancel as a lover. Pycelle drops his frail act in private with Ros. Littlefinger and Varys trade barbs about ambition and the throne.

At Winterfell Bran dreams again of the three-eyed raven flying into the crypts. He and Osha go down; Rickon and Shaggydog are already there—Rickon had the same dream. Outside, Maester Luwin’s face tells them Ned is dead.

In the Riverlands Catelyn receives the northern lords’ condolences, then breaks down alone in the woods. She finds Robb destroying a tree with his sword in grief. They embrace; she promises revenge after they free the girls. At a war council the lords debate allying with Stannis or Renly. Greatjon Umber declares the North was independent before the dragons and will not bow to southern kings now that the dragons are gone. He names Robb the King in the North. The others take up the cry and swear fealty. Catelyn visits the captive Jaime; he taunts her, admits pushing Bran, and says there are no men like him. She hits him with a rock.

At Tywin’s camp the capture of Jaime is a disaster. They now face Robb, Stannis, and Renly. Tyrion points out Ned’s execution ended any chance of easy peace. Tywin decides to fall back to Harrenhal, send Gregor to burn the Riverlands, and dispatch Tyrion to King’s Landing as Acting Hand to control Joffrey and Cersei (and kill schemers if needed). He orders Tyrion to leave Shae behind. Tyrion defies him and takes her anyway.

At the Wall Jon learns of Ned’s death and tries to desert to join Robb. Sam, Grenn, and Pyp stop him and recite the oath. He returns. Mormont overlooks it and tells him the real war is coming from beyond the Wall—wildlings, White Walkers, wights. He will lead a great ranging to learn the truth and find Benjen. Jon recommits.

In the Dothraki Sea Daenerys wakes to learn her son Rhaego was born dead and monstrously deformed. Most of the khalasar has left. Drogo lives but is a vacant shell. Mirri Maz Duur reveals her revenge: the Dothraki destroyed her temple and people; she has taken Drogo’s mind and the child’s life so the Stallion Who Mounts the World will never conquer. Daenerys tends the empty Drogo, then smothers him out of mercy. She builds a funeral pyre, places the dragon eggs on it, and has Mirri bound to the wood. She frees any remaining slaves and invites the few loyal ones to stay as equals. Ignoring Jorah’s pleas, she lights the pyre and walks into the flames. At dawn the fire is ash. Daenerys sits unharmed amid the embers, naked and soot-covered, with three living baby dragons—one on her shoulder, one on her arm, one climbing her leg. Jorah and the remaining Dothraki kneel. The dragons are reborn. The Mother of Dragons rises.
